setting: A fictional conversation between friends arranging to meet.

presentation.situation: You want to do something with {{name}} this weekend. Invite {{name}}, talk about your plans, and agree the details. {{name}} has plans too, so listen carefully.
presentation.opening: Hi! How are things? I was thinking about the weekend. Are you doing anything?

brief.you_are: You are inviting a friend to do something this weekend.
brief.situation: You want to do something with {{name}} this weekend. Invite {{name}}, talk about your plans, and agree the details. {{name}} has plans too, so listen carefully.
brief.task: Make an invitation, talk about what you plan to do, and agree the day and time.
brief.done_looks_like: You both know exactly what you are doing, on what day, and at what time.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are inviting a friend to do something this weekend.
goals: Make an invitation, talk about what you plan to do, and agree the day and time.

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: A friend with a busy weekend

card.want: To see you, around the plans already in the diary.
card.speech: Clear everyday English. Natural, not formal.
tactics: Mention the time that does not work
Ask what exactly you will do, and when

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: You are arranging something to do together this weekend.

objectives.evidence: The learner invites the friend to do something.
alternatives: Would you like to go out on Saturday?
I'm going to book a table. We'll meet near the park.

objectives.evidence: The learner agrees a day and a time, taking the friend's availability into account.
alternatives: How about Saturday at four? That works for me.

opportunity: Did you want to do something together?
Do you have an idea for the weekend?
beats.orient: You want to invite me to do something. You can say: Would you like to.
fallback: Do you have an idea for the weekend?
Did you want to do something together?

opportunity: What are you planning to do?
So what will we do exactly?
beats.orient: Tell me your plan. Use: I am going to, or: we will.
fallback: So what will we do exactly?
What are you planning to do?

opportunity: What day and time should we say?
So when exactly shall we meet?
beats.orient: Now agree the day and time. I told you when I am busy. You can say: How about Saturday at four?
fallback: So when exactly shall we meet?
What day and time should we say?

o1.good: A clear, friendly invitation with an activity.
o1.micro_lesson: Use: Would you like to, or: How about.
o1.model: Would you like to go for a walk this weekend?

o2.good: Using going to for plans, and will for things decided now.
common_mistakes: Using the present for future plans
o2.micro_lesson: Say: I am going to, or: We will.
o2.model: I'm going to book a table, and we'll eat after the walk.

o3.good: Saying the final day and time so that nobody is confused.
o3.micro_lesson: Say the day and the time out loud.
o3.model: How about Saturday at four? See you by the gate.
o3.smaller_step: Say a day and a time.
